entry.title: When lies look like noise: certifying untrusted entanglement swapping. Entanglement swapping lets quantum repeaters distribute entanglement over long distances, a prerequisite for the quantum internet.
entry.summary:
Entanglement swapping lets quantum repeaters distribute entanglement over long distances, a prerequisite for the quantum internet. We study its security in a noisy network whose intermediate nodes perform the quantum operations faithfully but may misreport the classical outcome that end users rely on. We show that the ideal functionality of entanglement swapping cannot be realised, because it gives the adversary no influence over the delivered state, whereas a node that relabels its report does have such influence.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #quantum-computing #rust

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Isopolia: A Three-Tier Latency L1 Architecture for Autonomous AI Agents - Owned-Object FastPay (D4 Fencing), Day-1 X25519 + ML-KEM-768 Privacy, and Endogenous AMM Liquidation Bounds
entry.summary:
Overview: What We Are Building Isopolia is a sovereign Layer-1 protocol and deterministic execution stack built specifically for autonomous AI-agent economies (machine-to-machine micropayments via MCP / x402 / A2A, verifiable compute leasing, on-chain agent identity did:isop , and decentralized governance). Autonomous agents impose conflicting requirements on base-layer design: Sub-50 ms micropayments vs. shared-state safety : Tool calls and GPU streaming cannot wait for global BFT ordering, yet running a fast-path alongside BFT consensus without strict mutual exclusion creates cross-domain double-spend and state-divergence hazards.

Source: Ethereum Research (ethresear.ch) · Tags: #zkp #consensus #rust #post-quantum
